establishes: The parity-odd CANDIDATES of curvature_invariants_parity_gate were not all tensor contractions. Eight of them summed a repeated index over two LOWER or two UPPER slots with no metric between them, which makes the value COORDINATE-DEPENDENT. Under a change of chart x = A y with A in SL(n, Z) those candidates move. The published D = 6 count of 2 came entirely from two of them. With every candidate repaired the counts are 1 in D = 4 at weight 6 and 0 in D = 6, where rankV = 0 -- every candidate, algebraic and derivative, Weyl-built and Riemann-built, is identically zero.
retracts: REVERSE_PHYSICS_PARITY_FIELD_EQUATIONS_V1 outright. The Lagrangian it differentiated is not a scalar.
corrects: REVERSE_PHYSICS_PARITY_CONFORMAL_COUNT_V1, in two of its four rows.

why_no_existing_check_could_catch_it.the_conformal_test_is_vacuous_on_weyl_bu: it compares g with e^{2 sigma} g where sigma vanishes at the base point. But C^{a}_{bcd} is conformally invariant with NO derivative-of-sigma terms at all, so ANY product of Weyl tensors, contracted in ANY index pattern, passes it automatically. The parity gate's own comment called these candidates 'conformally invariant by construction'. That was true, and it is exactly why the test could say nothing.
why_no_existing_check_could_catch_it.the_weight_count_cancels: the two mismatched pairs were one down-down and one up-up, contributing -2 and +2. Total weight -6, precisely correct.
why_no_existing_check_could_catch_it.the_actual_gap: nothing in the apparatus ever asked whether a candidate was a TENSOR. It tested conformal behaviour and never tested covariance.
why_no_existing_check_could_catch_it.where_the_defect_lives: each operand is a SLOT SPEC -- which slots feed the epsilon, which take a contracted index -- and its VARIANCE is implicit in which pre-raised array the spec is handed. cu012 is C^{abc}_{d}; cu01 is C^{ab}_{cd}. Pass the wrong one, or transpose two free slots, and the spec still type-checks, still runs, and still returns a number.

the_falsifier.construction: change chart by x = A y with A in SL(n, Z), so g'_{ab}(y) = A^k_a A^l_b g_{kl}(A y). A genuine scalar takes the same value at the base point in both charts.
the_falsifier.why_SL_and_not_GL: det A = 1 keeps the arithmetic exact and preserves |det g| = 1 at the base point -- which is what keeps the Levi-Civita SYMBOL equal to the TENSOR there, and the whole parity-odd sector rational.
the_falsifier.three_charts: unit lower-triangular, unit upper-triangular, and their PRODUCT, which is triangular in neither direction. Agreement across all three is agreement under a generic element rather than under a shear in one direction.
the_falsifier.calibrated_in_both_directions: R, C_{abcd}C^{abcd} and the PONTRYAGIN DENSITY must transport correctly and Pontryagin must be nonzero; a deliberately malformed sum_{ab} R_{ab} R_{ab} must MOVE. Without the negative half, 'everything passed' would mean the test is blind rather than the code correct.
the_falsifier.the_witness: sw0 as written is 6566972251/160 in one chart and -200078513393/160 in another. That first number is exactly the L(g) that REVERSE_PHYSICS_PARITY_FIELD_EQUATIONS_V1 published as its conformal-invariance control.

the_one_worth_naming: D = 6 candidate 9 was ZERO AS WRITTEN, so no wrong number ever pointed at it. It could only be found by asking whether the contraction was well formed -- never by watching output. Repairing it can turn a zero into a nonzero, so it had to be fixed BEFORE 'D = 6 is empty' meant anything.
why_the_D6_zero_is_structural: the covariant repairs vanish for RIEMANN as well as for Weyl. Riemann is not traceless, so this is the index PATTERN vanishing rather than the Weyl trace conditions, and no choice of curvature tensor rescues it.

an_empty_sector_is_a_result.the_problem: with the D = 6 sector empty, three of the parity gate's checks could no longer pass: they demanded that the candidates be nonzero, that the Weyl-built candidates be nonzero, and that the ranks saturate. Every one of those is a PREMISE OF A NONZERO COUNT, and demanding them would be demanding the wrong answer.
an_empty_sector_is_a_result.the_fix: checks 4, 5, 6 and 8 now branch on whether the sector is expected empty. Where it is, they require every candidate to be EXACTLY zero, both ranks to be zero (stronger than the count being zero, which is a difference and could vanish with both ranks positive), and a PARITY-EVEN witness to be nonzero.
an_empty_sector_is_a_result.the_parity_even_witness: R_{abcd} R^{abcd}, computed on the same fixtures. Without it, 'every parity-odd candidate vanishes' is indistinguishable from a pipeline that returns zero for everything. It is a new diagnostic slot added for exactly this.

does_not_establish: that no parity-odd conformal invariant exists in D = 6. The enumeration is exhaustive over one epsilon and three UNDIFFERENTIATED curvature tensors. The DERIVATIVE patterns -- eps grad R grad R and eps R grad grad R -- are a different space and are NOT swept. The parity gate finds its own derivative candidates zero, but that is a hand-built list again, and hand-built lists are exactly what failed here.

the claim that RP-PARITY is VACUOUS in D = 6. That is the reading the evidence favours, and it is the opposite direction from the retracted certificate's 'load-bearing'. It follows only if the candidate family is complete, which the line above says it is not. Recorded as a reading, not as a result.

that the CONTROL sweeps are as exhaustive as the curvature ones. The (2,2,2) restriction is justified BY the first Bianchi identity, so it is sound for Weyl and Riemann, which satisfy it, and NOT for the Bianchi-violating controls -- for those, patterns handing three or more slots to the epsilon are not swept. The control statements are about that subspace and are weaker than the curvature result.

the_d6_zero_is_now_a_count_not_a_lower_b.what_changed: the D = 6 zero was established over a HAND-BUILT candidate list, which is the same weakness that admitted the eight malformed candidates. It is now enumerated mechanically: 3240 patterns per metric, swept whole, over two fixtures.
the_d6_zero_is_now_a_count_not_a_lower_b.the_space: one epsilon (6 lower indices in D = 6) against three curvature tensors (12 slots): six slots feed the epsilon and six pair off, so C(12,6) x 15 = 13860 patterns. The FIRST BIANCHI IDENTITY -- verified in the gate as an exact componentwise identity rather than sampled -- forces the epsilon split to be exactly (2,2,2), because epsilon antisymmetrises everything it touches and C^{[abc]d} = 0 annihilates any tensor handing it three or more slots. That leaves 6^3 x 15 = 3240. All 15 matchings are swept, not only the 8 without self-pairs, so tracelessness is exercised rather than assumed.
the_d6_zero_is_now_a_count_not_a_lower_b.variance_is_derived_not_chosen: sixteen variance variants are precomputed by bitmask and each pattern selects its operands by raising exactly the slots it needs -- the epsilon slots, and one end of each contracted pair. Nothing is hand-written, which is precisely the discipline whose absence caused the defect this certificate corrects.
the_d6_zero_is_now_a_count_not_a_lower_b.result: every Weyl pattern and every Riemann pattern is exactly zero; rank of both families is 0

the_mechanism.finding: THE PAIR-EXCHANGE SYMMETRY C_{abcd} = C_{cdab} is what empties the sector.
the_mechanism.what_it_is_not: NOT the first Bianchi identity and NOT tracelessness. The pair-symmetric control violates Bianchi (verified in the gate) and is not traceless, and still vanishes on every pattern. And antisymmetry within each pair is not sufficient on its own -- 2208 patterns survive it.
the_mechanism.a_hypothesis_that_was_wrong_twice: Bianchi was asserted as the mechanism twice, once in the control design and once after the first run. Both were wrong. Neither reached a certificate because the control was built to be able to refute it -- which is the whole argument for a control that CAN fail.
